descriptionChirho: To move about aimlessly without a fixed course, describing physical wandering of persons or animals (Qal).
To stray from the right path in a moral or spiritual sense, erring from God's ways or truth (Qal).
To totter or reel as if intoxicated, describing unsteady physical movement often caused by drunkenness or divine judgment (Qal/Nifal).
To cause someone to wander from the right way, whether by deception, false teaching, or divine judgment; the causative counterpart of going astray (Hifil).
To be misled or deceived, the passive experience of being caused to err (Nifal).
